hero.title: Personal wellbeing, team workflows and Decision Intelligence research
hero.subtitle: Dzvin.co is an in-development digital wellbeing platform with personal support tools, an emerging permissioned team-analytics experience and a Decision Intelligence in Mental Health research direction using QDIP. There are no completed customer pilots or validated effectiveness results yet; the next stage is designed to test these hypotheses.
hero.note: All charts below are illustrative examples based on existing product capabilities, not live customer data.

blueprint.title: Three service tracks of one platform
blueprint.subtitle: The project is developing three connected experiences: private personal support, permissioned organization workflows and a research environment. Their integrated launch has not yet been qualified.

personalFlow.title: Personal support track
personalFlow.description: For individuals, the service brings daily check-ins, a diary and exercises into one space that is easy to return to.
personalFlow.focus: Focus: continuous personal support, short feedback loops and visible progress.

corporateFlow.title: Company pilot
corporateFlow.description: For companies, roles, groups and aggregated team indicators are in development — without access to employees' personal records.
corporateFlow.focus: Focus: employee support, aggregated data and clear access boundaries.

researchFlow.title: Research validation track
researchFlow.description: For research programs, institutes and universities, the service connects cohorts, outcome measurement and evidence accumulation to validate hypotheses.
researchFlow.focus: Focus: impact validation, repeatable observations and accountable program reporting.

b2c.title: For individuals
b2c.description: The personal service gathers state signals, offers simple practices and helps reveal what actually supports mental well-being in everyday use.

serviceSummaryItems.tracking: Brings state signals into one sequence.
serviceSummaryItems.support: Gives access to short practices in the guide whenever you need them.
serviceSummaryItems.consistency: Keeps change history easy to revisit.

resultSummaryItems.one: State becomes easier to understand over time.
resultSummaryItems.two: A short practice is only a few taps away.
resultSummaryItems.three: Support turns into a path that is easy to continue every day.

before.title: The problem we aim to address

one.title: Separate signals without a shared picture
one.description: Mood, short notes and self-checks existed separately, so it was difficult to see change as one continuous process.

two.title: Practices were not linked to the moment
two.description: Helpful exercises or advice could exist on their own, but they did not appear at the exact moment they were most relevant.

three.title: Results did not accumulate in one story
three.description: Even when something helped, it did not turn into a support path people could quickly return to.

tracking.title: State is captured in one place
tracking.description: Mood, short notes and questionnaires are gathered into one sequence that shows frequency of change, recurring triggers and movement across days.

support.title: Practices always at hand
support.description: Breathing, calming, meditations and tips are collected in the guide — you choose what to try right now.

consistency.title: Effective routines are easy to repeat
consistency.description: Saved exercises, materials and state history stay available so people can repeat what has already produced a visible result.

one.title: Review personal changes over time
one.description: The intended timeline shows repeated observations when users contribute data. Whether this improves awareness still requires evaluation.

two.title: Make a next step accessible
two.description: The intended flow offers a clear optional practice following a check-in; its appropriateness and usefulness require user research.

three.title: Keep the support journey connected
three.description: The product aims to link exercises and history. A measurable effect on wellbeing has not been established.

outcomes.one: Review personal observations and discover possible patterns.
outcomes.two: Choose short, voluntary practices rather than having decisions imposed automatically.
outcomes.three: Follow your personal timeline; this approach still needs evidence of usefulness.

b2b.title: For companies
b2b.description: The B2B experience is being developed to show permissioned aggregate trends in stress, mood, energy and focus, supporting HR and managers in reviewing team-support priorities. Its practical benefit remains a hypothesis requiring security qualification and independent evaluation.

governance.title: Org structure, roles and accountability zones
governance.description: The platform brings teams, roles, groups and access scopes into one managed layer so managers can see the right slice of the organization without permission chaos, manual reporting merges or endless clarification loops.

analytics.title: Team indicators from available observations
analytics.description: The planned view aggregates permitted stress, mood, energy and focus signals. Freshness and completeness depend on actual participation and configuration; production performance and reliability remain to be qualified.

decisionSupport.title: Context for support conversations
decisionSupport.description: Aggregated trends are intended to help HR and leaders discuss team support priorities. The system draws no automatic conclusions about individual people; the value of this approach still needs to be tested in pilots.

one.title: Planned team-support workflow
one.description: Once qualified, role-scoped group signals and documented follow-up may help teams organize wellbeing support. Measured outcomes are not yet available.

two.title: Hypothesis: more timely signal review
two.description: We plan to evaluate whether repeated observations and a managed workflow improve time to review. Reduced burnout and attrition have not been demonstrated.

three.title: Evidence to inform HR decisions
three.description: The research plan includes evaluating trends and agreed KPIs while avoiding causal claims without a suitable study design.

outcomes.one: Goal: an aggregated view of team well-being without exposing personal histories.
outcomes.two: Goal: a structured process for discussing team support.
outcomes.three: Goal: verifiable indicators for HR and leaders, agreed before the pilot starts.

rd.title: For researchers, institutes and universities
rd.description: The R&D workspace is being developed for research projects, cohorts, repeated observations and future evaluation of predictive and Decision Intelligence hypotheses. No scientific superiority or intervention effect has been established.

cohorts.title: Build comparable cohorts
cohorts.description: Unified collection instruments make it possible to build cohorts, compare subgroups and repeat an observation design across collection waves.

validation.title: Validate predictions
validation.description: The proposed forecast-to-observation loop is intended to support evaluation of calibration, drift and changes after action. Independent research outcomes are not yet available.

reporting.title: Report impact
reporting.description: Data can be turned into material for reports, ethics packages, grant applications and communication with organizations that finance research.

one.title: Collect standardized observations
one.description: We work with the same scales, behavioral signals and controlled data collection flows so results remain comparable.

two.title: Build cohorts and analytical cuts
two.description: Participants can be segmented by state patterns, risk, intervention response and observation windows.

three.title: We plan hypothesis evaluation
three.description: Together with partners we define in advance how hypotheses will be tested and which results count as meaningful. There are no independent results yet.

one.title: Repeatable measurement logic
one.description: The same measurement logic works in the everyday product and in the research layer, so data does not break across environments.

two.title: Transparent methodology
two.description: Protocols, samples and evaluation criteria are fixed before data collection so results can be reproduced and independently verified.

three.title: Evidence for papers and grants
three.description: Cohort comparisons, intervention dynamics and program outcomes accumulate into material that can support a publication or grant proposal.

one.title: Reduce time to a working study design
one.description: Teams do not start from zero: a working digital tool for daily self-assessments and a diary already exists and can be adapted to an agreed protocol.

two.title: Provide structure for reports and papers
two.description: Researchers get a consistent data structure from participants who gave separate consent, for analysis and accountable reporting.

three.title: Strengthen grant reasoning
three.description: We help explain what is measured, how effect is validated and why the approach is practically valuable for a research team or grant provider.

one.title: Standardized inputs
one.description: Cohorts are built from the same self-checks, behavioral signals and questionnaires the platform already uses day to day.

two.title: Hypotheses checked against outcomes
two.description: Hypotheses are tested against predefined outcomes on separate, approved data — without conclusions the study design does not support.

three.title: An accountable evidence package
three.description: Aggregated trends, cohort comparisons and program results accumulate into an evidence base institutes, universities and research teams can actually use.

outcomes.one: A population-level view built from the same modules people use every day.
outcomes.two: An accumulating evidence base that confirms or refutes each program hypothesis.
outcomes.three: A path from intervention delivery to accountable outcome reporting.
